Because the monad is all mind, and we have the capacity to reject this world and return to the monad. Right? So why would he force us to do what we don't want to do? If you want to return to him, then you have the choice to engage in spirituality, goodness, and knowledge, which will allow you to return to him. That's the first explanation.

The second explanation is from Dante: The monad is eternal, perfect, and immutable, thus lacking imagination. But how do beings grow? Through imagination. To continue growing, the monad allowed the demiurge to create human beings because humans are flawed, make mistakes, and commit evil. These actions expand the universe's imagination, allowing the monad to expand.

So in this perspective, each time we imagine or commit mistakes, we turn to the monad. When we recognize these mistakes and adjust, we expand the monad’s imagination. Secret societies believe that evil and good exist together; you can only be good by doing evil because committing evil gives you a chance to become better.

We're doing Paradise Lost, which is the national epic of the British Empire. If you are an elite member of the empire, you memorize this poem, as it becomes part of your soul. Written by John Milton, who was a rebel and freethinker, fighting for free speech and blind from birth, he dictated his work to secretaries. His poetry is considered divine truth.

John Milton's Paradise Lost is foundational to many secret societies, containing the secrets of the universe. To see these secrets embedded in the text, you must understand them yourself. The plot of Paradise Lost is simple: it reimagnines the fall of man with Satan tricking Eve. After a war against God, Satan and devils are banished to hell. They discuss their options, proposing either creating an empire or sitting back. Determined to seek vengeance, Satan plans to corrupt Adam and Eve in the Garden of Eden, destroying humanity forever.
